question: The elliptical shapes in temple architecture in Dravidian style are known by which of the given terms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gajaprishta**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gajaprishta**, also known as the "Elephant-back style," refers to the elliptical or apsidal design often seen in Dravidian temple architecture.
 
• It is primarily used for constructing the sanctum (garbhagriha) and resembles the shape of an elephant's back.
 
• Such a design is prominent in South Indian temples, especially in ancient Chola, Pallava, and Pandya constructions.
 
• The Gajaprishta style adds structural stability and a unique aesthetic to the temples, emphasizing the harmonious blend of form and functionality.
 
• Examples of temples with Gajaprishta architecture include the Kailasanathar Temple in Kanchipuram and certain structures in Aihole, Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vritta:** Refers to circular or spherical structures, often used in Buddhist stupas rather than Hindu temples.
 
• **Nasi:** Represents the ornamental projection or arch above the temple doorways, commonly seen in North Indian (Nagara) architecture.
 
• **Ayatasra:** Indicates rectangular or square designs used for temple layouts, often seen in Dravidian temples but distinct from apsidal forms.
 
• **Dravidian Style:** A prominent architectural style in South India, characterized by pyramid-shaped towers (vimanas), intricate sculptures, and large temple complexes.
 
• **Temple Architecture in India:** Broadly divided into three styles: Nagara (North Indian), Dravidian (South Indian), and Vesara (a mix of both styles).
